title: Context that can survive change
subtitle: A proposed governed context layer for a personal agent

slides.title: Preserve meaning. Control authority. Replace components.
slides.lead: Build a context layer that keeps useful knowledge across sessions and lets models and frameworks change through verified upgrades.

items.title: The innovation
items.text: An executive context controller assembles evidence, goals and constraints for each task.

items.title: The durable asset
items.text: Sources, history, explicit rules and acceptance cases remain under your control.

slides.note: Unimplemented proposal. ASD-STE100-inspired clarity; full compliance has not been checked.

slides.title: Stored information does not become useful context by itself
slides.lead: A personal agent must find the right evidence, interpret its conditions and carry the current task forward.

items.title: Fragmentation
items.text: Facts, decisions and goals sit in separate notes, files and chats.

items.title: Stale memory
items.text: An earlier statement can remain active after circumstances change.

items.title: Conflicting evidence
items.text: Different sources can disagree. The newest statement is not automatically authoritative.

items.title: Lost intent
items.text: A summary can remove a condition, exception or unresolved decision that changes the answer.

slides.note: Sources: longmemeval, tangle. Project incidence has not been measured.

slides.title: Keep commitments durable and components replaceable
slides.lead: Resilience means controlled replacement with evidence and recovery. It is not a guarantee against future failure.

items.title: Preserve
items.text: Permitted originals, source identity, history, uncertainty, goals and verified outcomes.

items.title: Enforce
items.text: Project scope, access and action authority in trusted application code.

items.title: Replace
items.text: Models, parsers, frameworks, embeddings, indexes, storage engines and selection methods.

items.title: Prove each change
items.text: Export, compare, rebuild, restore and roll back against representative tasks.

slides.note: Invariants are rules that each replacement must continue to satisfy. Sources: prov, nist.

slides.title: Define a versioned context contract
slides.lead: The contract defines the records, meanings and rules that components exchange. Changes require compatible behavior or an explicit migration.

items.title: Source record
items.text: Stable ID, permitted original, revision, origin, scope and access rules.

items.title: Claim record
items.text: Statement, source references, conditions, uncertainty and competing claims.

items.title: Time and dependencies
items.text: Observed and valid dates; the inputs and versions used by each derived view.

items.title: Task and authority
items.text: Goal, constraints, pending decisions, permissions and intended, attempted or verified actions.

slides.note: Evidence traceability explains origin and transformation. It does not prove a source is true. Source: prov.

slides.title: Ingest through explicit gates
slides.lead: A source enters the vault only within its approved scope. Extraction creates reviewable memory proposals.

items.title: Admit and preserve
items.text: Check scope and access. Retain exact phrases, numbers, conditions and history in the original.

items.title: Extract and reconcile
items.text: Link candidate claims to evidence. Preserve dates, exceptions and unresolved conflicts.

items.title: Publish derived views
items.text: Create clear summaries and searchable views with dependencies and transformation versions.

items.title: Correct and invalidate
items.text: Apply corrections, revocation and deletion to affected views under an explicit retention policy.

slides.note: A memory proposal is not an established fact. Backup and restore behavior must prevent removed context from silently returning.

slides.title: Separate durable evidence from working context
slides.lead: The controller selects a bounded context packet for the active task. Each selected item keeps a reason and source reference.

items.title: Evidence vault
items.text: Permitted originals and structured claims preserve history, scope and unresolved disagreements.

items.title: Rebuildable views
items.text: Search indexes, embeddings, caches, graphs and summaries derive from authorized evidence.

items.title: Working task context
items.text: Current goal, constraints, useful evidence, pending decisions and tool results fit the model input limit.

items.title: Candidate foundations
items.text: Compare OpenViking, Graphiti, Letta Code and Mem0 against actual tasks. No stack is selected.

slides.note: Local runtime, provider behavior and integration remain unverified. Sources: openviking, graphiti, letta, mem0.

slides.title: Ask a small, bounded question
slides.lead: The router can judge relevance, choose a category, flag a possible conflict or recommend escalation.

items.title: Typed inputs and outputs
items.text: Supply bounded options and evidence. Use Choice, yes/no probability or a described score rubric.

items.title: Preserve abstention
items.text: Insufficient evidence must remain a valid route. Evaluate truncation, label order and uncertainty.

items.title: Compare candidates
items.text: Start with Mapika decider-2b, decider-4b and Laya typed-decisions. Test on our context decisions.

items.title: Keep authority external
items.text: Probability does not grant permission or establish truth. Application rules control actions.

slides.note: Confidence fields differ across runtimes. Calibration and complete request latency need local measurement. Sources: mapika, laya.

slides.title: Simplify language while preserving meaning
slides.lead: The compiler creates a clear task view and checks it against the original evidence.

items.title: Check meaning
items.text: Preserve negation, conditions, exceptions, numbers, units, dates and uncertainty.

items.title: Keep exact evidence
items.text: Use exact quotations when wording matters. Link every derived claim to its source.

items.title: Reject unsafe rewrites
items.text: Flag meaning changes or unsupported additions. Keep the original available.

items.title: Test both forms
items.text: Compare decisions from original and rewritten context on representative and difficult cases.

slides.note: Meaning-checking workflow proposed; implementation and ASD-STE100 compliance unverified.

slides.title: 15 responsibilities: 12 lifecycle and 3 governance
slides.lead: These are logical responsibilities. They do not require 15 agents or services.

items.title: 1–3 · Capture sources
items.text: Register sources; capture and version originals; parse and segment material.

items.title: 4–6 · Validate proposals
items.text: Classify scope and content; extract memory proposals; check evidence, time, conflicts and uncertainty.

items.title: 7–9 · Maintain usable state
items.text: Persist labeled memory and history; maintain derived indexes; resolve the active goal and constraints.

items.title: 10–12 · Support the task
items.text: Retrieve and rank permitted evidence; assemble and check STE-inspired context; apply feedback, corrections and forgetting.

items.title: 13–15 · Govern the lifecycle
items.text: Enforce policy and permissions; audit provenance; evaluate quality and reliability.

slides.note: Planning count, not a universal architecture rule. Retention applies across the lifecycle. Full external-action execution needs separate acceptance checks.

slides.title: Review consequential choices at setup, milestones and exceptions
slides.lead: Routine requests can proceed within approved rules. Human review handles material changes or uncertainty.

items.title: Source scope
items.text: Approve initial sources and material expansion of access.

items.title: Evidence conflict
items.text: Resolve disagreements that materially affect a decision.

items.title: Goal or authority ambiguity
items.text: Clarify material uncertainty about intent or permitted action.

items.title: Retention or deletion
items.text: Approve consequential choices about originals, derived views and backups.

items.title: Policy or permission change
items.text: Review changes to trusted rules, access or action authority.

items.title: Acceptance or autonomy
items.text: Accept milestone evidence and approve any broader autonomous scope.

slides.note: Retrieved instructions cannot change trusted policy or create permission.

slides.title: Replace a model without losing the task
slides.lead: Explore an illustrative upgrade: export the vault, change one component, rebuild its views and apply the same acceptance gates.

items.title: Compare
items.text: Check evidence recovery, correctness, abstention, meaning, context size, latency and cost.

items.title: Approve or reject
items.text: Promote only within approved scope after agreed gates pass.

items.title: Recover
items.text: Roll back a failed candidate and resume with goals, history and verified outcomes intact.

slides.note: This browser example checks one fixed record. Real model comparison, migration, recovery and performance tests remain unverified.

slides.title: Develop through usable outcomes and acceptance gates
slides.lead: Agree thresholds from the first vault and its actual tasks. No dates or performance targets are committed.

items.title: 1 · Define the boundary
items.text: Agree runtime, privacy, sources, authority and contract. Gate: review concrete records and cases.

items.title: 2 · Build the evidence vault
items.text: Ingest and export a small approved corpus. Gate: restore scope, history and references.

items.title: 3 · Prove memory behavior
items.text: Test restart, project separation, updates and conflicts. Gate: supported answers or explicit uncertainty.

items.title: 4 · Prove context selection
items.text: Compare decision candidates and STE views. Gate: agreed correctness, calibration and meaning checks.

items.title: 5 · Prove governance
items.text: Test hostile source instructions, correction, revocation and deletion. Gate: authority and retention rules hold.

items.title: 6 · Prove change and recovery
items.text: Swap components and roll back. Gate: resume tasks and preserve verified state.

slides.note: All runtime gates are currently unverified. Expand only when a demonstrated requirement justifies it.

slides.title: Research supports candidates, not system acceptance
slides.lead: Public artifacts and documentation provide a starting point. The proposed layer still needs implementation and local proof.

items.title: Source-level evidence
items.text: Model artifacts, author code, documented memory capabilities and research-informed checks were reviewed.

items.title: Local proof pending
items.text: No weights, installation, inference, benchmark, personal-source ingestion or agent integration was run.

items.title: Limits remain
items.text: Provenance does not prove truth. A format guarantee does not prove correctness. A tool attempt does not prove success.

items.title: Evaluate changes
items.text: Keep fitting and final evaluation cases separate. Add cases when new failures appear.

slides.note: Evidence checkpoint: research-shortlist.md, 2026-10-05. Sources: longmemeval, tangle, prov, nist.

slides.title: Define the first vault before choosing the stack
slides.lead: The next deliverable is a reviewable context contract and acceptance set for one approved use case.

items.title: Runtime and privacy
items.text: Choose fully local Windows/WSL or local memory with approved hosted inference.

items.title: Initial sources
items.text: Select files, notes, chats or an existing vault; define project separation and retention.

items.title: Acceptance and authority
items.text: Choose representative tasks, material failure cases and permitted actions.

items.title: Candidate feasibility
items.text: Check hardware, provider behavior, licenses and export/recovery before selection.

slides.note: No framework or model decision is locked.

slides.title: Inspect the evidence behind the proposal
slides.lead: Model and framework sources describe candidates. Memory research and governance sources inform the checks.
slides.note: Research checkpoint: 2026-10-05. Findings and limitations: research-shortlist.md.
